questions.q: What was God's first recorded response to Elijah's exhaustion (1 Kings 19:5–7)?
questions.explanation: 'Arise and eat, for the journey is too great for you.' Only afterwards came the journey, the mountain and the whisper.

questions.q: What is the default for food on this retreat?
questions.explanation: The retreat does not require fasting. You can complete every session with full benefit while eating normally, and fasting is deliberately placed here so no one feels it is expected.

questions.q: For whom does the chapter say food fasting is not recommended, without exception?
options: Anyone with a current or past eating disorder or disordered-eating pattern
Anyone who has never fasted before
questions.explanation: Fasting can reawaken patterns under a spiritual disguise. Do not substitute another restrictive plan under a different spiritual name; follow your established meal plan and treatment guidance.

questions.q: What does Isaiah 58 teach about fasting?
options: Religious self-denial is empty when separated from justice, generosity, humility and care for the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Scripture treats fasting as a recognised practice but not as a technique for extracting things from God.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about sleep during the retreat?
options: Set a 5 a.m. alarm to prove your seriousness
Sleep is a gift (Psalm 127:2); if you arrive exhausted you may spend much of Day 1 asleep, and that is fine
Sleep is time stolen from the retreat
Nap only after completing all sessions
questions.explanation: Elijah slept twice before God spoke. Keep your normal sleep routine and medication, and do not use the retreat to fix your sleep.

questions.q: What is the chapter's rule about movement?
options: Train hard to burn off stress
Avoid all movement to stay still
questions.explanation: Gentle movement within your ability and near help is what the retreat needs. The point is a change of position and place, not distance.

reflection: Food plan: will you follow your normal eating pattern? If you are considering a food fast, is it already a healthy, established practice for you, and have you obtained appropriate medical guidance?
What will you eat, and how will you get it? Write a simple meal plan for each day.
What time will you allow yourself to sleep and wake?
What movement, if any, will you include, and where is it safe?
